item.title: Drought, fire and high diesel prices 'addin' up tough' for Oregon ranchers
item.description:
News
Drought, fire and high diesel prices 'addin' up tough' for Oregon ranchers
October 25, 202612:01 AM ET
By
Anna King
Katie Baltzor rides her side-by-side among the black angus cattle she raises near her home outside of Hines, Oregon.
Anna King/NWPB
hide caption
toggle caption i
Anna King/NWPB
HARNEY COUNTY, ORE. - Late bloomin' rabbitbrush – wads of swaying ochre – stud the roadsides and steep eroded-basalt buttes rising up from the basin floor outside of Hines, Oregon.
In a broad open field, horses munch standing hay as Katie Baltzor watches her black angus cattle on this fall day.
We've ridden out here in a side-by-side vehicle – it's like an overgrown golf cart with a pickup bed in the back made for rough ranch work.
All the animals are quiet. Happy. With their heads down grazing.
"You see that horse, how he's got speckled colors?" said Baltzor with a smile in her voice. "Looks like country gravy, I guess that's why they called him Gravy."
Diesel prices remain near record highs, despite recent actions by President Trump as the mid-term elections get closer.

item.description:

Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement over sexual abuse claims
October 24, 20266:47 PM ET
By
Chandelis Duster
St. Patrick's Cathedral in Manhattan, the seat of the Archdiocese of New York, holds mass on April 21, 2025, in New York.
Yuki Iwamura/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Yuki Iwamura/AP
The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to pay $800 million to settle the claims brought against the church by some 1,300 people who say they faced sexual abuse from clergy members and lay workers.
Jeff Anderson, a lawyer whose firm represents more than 250 of the plaintiffs, said the settlement was finalized, pending signed paperwork, and that all plaintiffs had agreed to the settlement.
In an email sent to priests of the archdiocese on Saturday afternoon and shared with NPR, Archbishop Ronald Hicks also said the deal had not yet been signed but that an agreement had been reached with plaintiffs and their attorneys.
"We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors," Hicks wrote in the email. item.title: Gunmen open fire at a church during a funeral in Jordan, killing 7 and wounding 40
item.description:
Middle East
Gunmen open fire at a church during a funeral in Jordan, killing 7 and wounding 40
October 24, 20267:59 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
A man looks through a gap in a stone wall toward a Greek Orthodox church where gunmen opened fire during a funeral hours earlier in Hamoud village, in Jordan's Karak governorate on Friday.
AP Photo/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
AP Photo/AP
JERUSALEM — Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said.
The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 90 kilometers (55 miles) south of the capital, Amman.
Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man who appears to be holding a semiautomatic rifle then approaches and opens fire, and all three then run toward the church.
Video footage taken by witnesses shows broken glass and pools of blood on the floor of the church.
Dorgham Halasa, who was among the mourners inside the church, said intense gunfire erupted 15 minutes after the funeral had started, and then people started running. "It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire," Halasa said.

item.title: U.S. birth rate drops to record low, but older women are having more babies
item.description:
National
U.S. birth rate drops to record low, but older women are having more babies
October 24, 20266:00 AM ET
Brian Mann
Fewer women in their 20s are choosing to become mothers, leading to an overall birthrate decline in the U.S. But the birth rate among U.S. women age 30-45 is rising according to the latest federal data.
CHARLY TRIBALLEAU/AFP
hide caption
toggle caption i
CHARLY TRIBALLEAU/AFP
Sarah Harris was 36 years old when she gave birth to her daughter Bridget last year. She describes motherhood as equal parts joy and exhaustion. "When you have a baby in your mid-30s, what you gain in wisdom and experience you also lose in terms of energy," Harris says with a laugh.
Harris, who lives in Vermont, was laid off from a job four months after Bridget was born. She says she's still figuring out what her career and her life will look like with a child. Harris thinks a lot of women are like her. They're wrestling with financial uncertainty and waiting much later to choose pregnancy.
